name: CertChain
tagline: Decentralized certificate verification on Ethereum + IPFS
about: CertChain is a hybrid on-chain/off-chain decentralized application for issuing and verifying academic certificates. It combines Ethereum smart contracts with IPFS-backed decentralized storage through Pinata to create a tamper-evident, independently verifiable credential system.

architecture.summary: CertChain decouples file storage from cryptographic verification. Heavy credential assets are persisted via content-addressed IPFS storage, while tamper-evident SHA-256 digests and metadata hashes are permanently written to an Ethereum smart contract.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: CertChain is a decentralized application (DApp) designed to address the vulnerabilities and administrative friction inherent in traditional academic credentialing. By establishing an immutable audit trail on the Ethereum blockchain and persisting credential media on the InterPlanetary File System (IPFS), CertChain provides institutions and employers with a trustless verification mechanism that operates independently of any central issuing authority.

sections.heading: The Problem
sections.body:
Traditional academic credentials suffer from significant structural weaknesses. Physical paper certificates are susceptible to forgery, loss, and physical degradation. Digital PDF certificates can be altered using basic editing software, and existing background check procedures require contacting issuing universities directly—a manual, labor-intensive process that can take weeks.

Centralized certificate registries also present single-point-of-failure risks: if an issuing institution shuts down, rebrands, or experiences server outages, historical student credentials can become unprovable.

sections.heading: Why Blockchain?
sections.body:
Public blockchains provide an append-only, tamper-proof state ledger. When an issuing authority records a cryptographic digest of a certificate on Ethereum, that record cannot be modified, deleted, or backdated by any actor—including the university itself.

By anchoring certificates to smart contracts, verification becomes decentralized and perpetual: employers and verification agencies can cryptographically validate credentials directly against the blockchain without requiring API keys, recurring subscriptions, or manual institutional correspondence.

sections.heading: System Architecture & Data Flows
sections.body: CertChain employs a hybrid on-chain/off-chain architecture to optimize both gas costs and storage permanence. Storing multi-megabyte PDF files directly on Ethereum is cost-prohibitive, so CertChain splits the data lifecycle into two synchronized pipelines: an off-chain content storage stream and an on-chain cryptographic ledger stream.

sections.heading: Certificate Issuance Workflow
sections.body:
The issuance pipeline begins when an authorized institutional administrator fills in student metadata and attaches the credential file via the React interface.

The Express backend receives the payload and streams the binary document directly to Pinata's IPFS pinning service, which returns an immutable Content Identifier (CID). Simultaneously, a SHA-256 cryptographic hash of the file and its associated metadata is computed. The administrator confirms the issuance transaction in MetaMask, executing a Solidity contract method that maps the unique Certificate ID to the cryptographic digest on Ethereum.

sections.heading: Three-Layer Verification Pipeline
sections.body:
Verification requires zero privileged access. An employer enters a Certificate ID or scans a certificate QR code. The system executes a three-layer validation check:

1. Smart contract query: Retrieves the registered issuer address, timestamp, and SHA-256 hash from the Ethereum blockchain.
2. IPFS content retrieval: Fetches the original certificate document from IPFS using the stored CID.
3. Cryptographic reconciliation: Recalculates the SHA-256 hash of the retrieved document on the client and compares it against the on-chain hash. If even a single byte has changed, the verification immediately fails.

sections.heading: Batch Issuance & Gas Optimization
sections.body:
Graduating classes often require issuing hundreds of credentials simultaneously. Submitting individual blockchain transactions for each student would result in excessive gas fees and repetitive wallet confirmations.

CertChain integrates PapaParse to parse batch CSV files on the frontend. The backend prepares batch records and executes multi-certificate issuance in single smart contract transactions, amortizing base transaction overhead and significantly reducing gas expenditures per student.

sections.heading: Security & Integrity Model
sections.body:
System integrity is enforced through cryptographic boundaries:

- Role-based smart contract permissions ensure only whitelisted institutional wallet addresses can invoke issuance functions.
- Content-addressing via IPFS guarantees that any modification to a hosted certificate produces an entirely different CID, immediately invalidating the link.
- Cryptographic SHA-256 hashing bridges off-chain storage with on-chain consensus, ensuring end-to-end immutability.

sections.heading: Technical Challenges & State Coordination
sections.body:
A central challenge was coordinating asynchronous operations across three disparate environments: client-side React UI state, Node.js backend streaming, and Ethereum network confirmations through MetaMask.

Blockchain transactions introduce unpredictable confirmation latencies and potential network rejections. The frontend was engineered with optimistic UI feedback, transaction status polling via Ethers.js, and graceful failure handling during IPFS uploads to prevent orphaned state.

sections.heading: Outcome & Project Impact
sections.body: CertChain demonstrates an end-to-end, production-grade Web3 application combining decentralized consensus with user-friendly web interfaces. The project showcases how blockchain and peer-to-peer storage can solve tangible real-world problems in academic verification, and was developed in the context of the Build with AI Solution Challenge 2026.
